root_cause.text: The `vxlan_na_create()` function fails to validate that the length field of ND options is within the remaining option area and that the source LLADDR option is large enough to contain an Ethernet address, allowing a malformed packet to cause out-of-bounds reads or memory access beyond the allocated buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "A malformed option can make the parser advance beyond the computed option span or use a too-short source LLADDR option payload." The patch adds two checks: `if (!ns->opt[i + 1] || i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen)` and `if ((ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >= sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN)`, which directly address the missing validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking in vxlan_na_create to prevent out-of-bounds access on malformed Neighbor Advertisement options.
intent_record.what: Added two safety checks in vxlan_na_create: (1) validate that the option offset computed from the length field does not exceed the total option length; (2) verify that the option length for ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR is at least the size of the option header plus ETH_ALEN before using its address.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds reads from malformed IPv6 Neighbor Advertisement options. The first check avoids skipping past the end of options; the second ensures the source link-layer address field is present and fully contained within the option.

candidates.rationale: The loop uses the option length field (ns->opt[i+1]) without verifying it is within the remaining buffer, allowing a malformed packet with a large length to cause out-of-bounds reads.
This check only catches a zero-length option but does not prevent an excessively long option length from being used, which can lead to out-of-bounds memory access.
When a source LLADDR option is found, this statement accesses its payload without verifying that the option length is sufficient to hold an Ethernet address, leading to potential out-of-bounds read.
